title: Kaze
description: Lying in the long grass in July, looking up past the stalks into a deep summer sky, and the wind is yours. Brush across the frame and your stroke becomes a gust: it runs on through the grass, the tall brome and seed heads lean over under it across the clouds and swing back with a little overshoot, and the clouds behind drift faster after it. Left alone, a light breeze keeps them moving.
intent: Technique 10, Kaze (factory/reality/techniques.md): an Eulerian motion field you author live. A 96x64 stable-fluids velocity grid (Stam 1999, https://www.dgp.toronto.edu/public_user/stam/reality/Research/pdf/ns.pdf) carries the air in metres per second over the whole frame; each cell's grass is a damped spring driven by dynamic pressure. The grass is geometry seen worm's-eye: a 116 deg stereographic lens 4 cm off the ground, pitched so the zenith sits just above the top of the frame, and every blade, culm and brome panicle a world-space ribbon rooted below the bottom edge, so the stalks run up and converge on that vanishing point, the nearest long, the field behind a low fringe. One tall culm with a seed head at your shoulder is the single sharp near-black anchor (full resolution, 4x MSAA) against the cumulus; the rest is drawn at half resolution, a touch diffused behind it, and lit against the light: a darker core, a thin warm yellow-green transmission rim on the edge toward the sun, and the sky's value let in with depth, so the field falls back softer, paler and bluer, and the low leaves across the middle are thinned so the cloud's base stands clear. Edges are the blades' own MSAA coverage, premultiplied, with no matte or alpha test; where a blade crosses the sun, a thin halation ring. The wind bends each stalk about its root: the bend read at its tip on screen moves it level in the world by the bend times its lever (length times height along it squared), and it comes down a little as it lies over. The cumulus drift is a two-phase flow map (Vlachos 2010), faster toward the zenith, and leans after the gusts. ?gust=demo throws a scripted gust, ?t=seconds runs the wind that long and holds it, ?breeze=0..2 scales the idle air, ?debug=bend tints the grass by its bend.

sources.author: Forest Service, Northern Region (USDA), via Wikimedia Commons
sources.note: No longer drawn: the grass is now geometry (grass.js), and this photograph only fixes the frame the sky and the wind grid share (its uv; the sun is since moved to the frame's top left corner). Tall grass against partly cloudy skies, Tally Lake Ranger District, Flathead National Forest, Montana: camera at blade height pitched up. Display P3 converted to sRGB, worked at 2400x1600. Sky matte by tools/depth/segment.py sky (colour unmixing for thin blades), firmed by colour (sunlit brome is greener than the sky behind it) and darkness, and by a dark-object prior (a thin line clearly darker or greener than the sky inpainted behind it by a grey closing is all blade, so the brome crossing the sun stands solid); the sky behind thin grass is that closing, so the cloud texture runs on round the sun, which rolls off to warm white with its diffusion baked above a threshold; grass colour unmixed against a push-pull sky so a F + (1 - a) S recomposes the photograph. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/kaze/bake.py. Its own sky.webp is since replaced by the HDRI sky below.

sources.author: Dimitrios Savva (photography), Jarod Guest (processing), Poly Haven
sources.note: The sky layer: a 3600x2400 pinhole view (43 deg) turned to the towering cauliflower cumulus over the HDRI's eastern horizon, pitched just above the gum trees (what is left of them below the frame painted out) and mirrored so the tower stands to the right behind the hero culms. The HDRI's own sun is hidden in the storm behind the camera, so the sun is a point of the frame: a tight warm white bloom in the top left corner with the cobalt saturated nearly up to it. Printed with a soft local shoulder; the cumulus through one monotone curve to warm white domes (about 245 on screen) with pale skylight-blue shade between and under them, its edges soft but defined; the open sky a zenith gradient from pale cyan (hue ~200) low in the frame to deep cobalt at the top. Replaces an earlier cut of Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Greg Zaal, Jarod Guest, CC0), whose flat overhead cumulus read as torn cotton. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/kaze/sky_hdri.py.
